correctness.rationale: The norm follows from optimal explicit mass transport and matching dual feasible potentials for every s>=1/2. All n orthants are integrated, with two imbalance sectors, a beta simplex integral and a Vandermonde identity; the dual is integrated via the exact sample-range density. Coefficient comparison using the binomial recurrence yields the signed derivative factor. Boundary s=1/2 and the limit s->infinity checked. Standalone VERIFY.py independently confirms uncollapsed rational orthant volumes and derivative coefficients for n=2..14 and numerical dual/primal convex hulls for n=2..5. No finite computation is substituted for the proof of all n and real s.

originality.rationale: The new claim computes both coordinate volumes and the entire dimension-uniform Mahler function and its strict equilateral optimum. The two verified full primary documents treat the extreme-molecule theorem and previously known general/endpoint volume-product theory respectively. Full text of the nearest matching published mathematical record evaluates Euclidean Banach-Mazur distance, not affine volume product. Actual published-finding corpus and web searches found no equivalent theorem; equivalence outside coverage remains possible.

value.rationale: A complete all-dimension affine volume-product profile for an intrinsic Banach-space family interpolating tree, equilateral and remote-hub regimes; strict and unique within-family maximizer proven by a nontrivial positive-coefficient derivative identity. This fills the gap between known endpoint evaluations and other geometric invariants of the same metric, and supplies exact quantitative results not implied by the existing extreme-molecule theorem. No general Mahler-maximality assertion is made.
